text:
elaine: Hey team — bringing up the new tiny-reranker (distill-v2-int8). Offline eval shows NDCG@10 down ~3.2% vs fp16 baseline but MRR@1 up 1.8%. Anyone seen this top1 vs tail inversion before?
ben: Hmm, interesting. MRR up while NDCG down usually means top1 improved but ranking beyond top1 got worse or ties shuffled.
priya: Could be candidate normalization or softmax scaling after quantization. Did you preserve scorer logits float->int calibration?
kai: Also check candidate ordering in the harness. If candidate canonicalization changed (de-dup, trimming), top1 could flip.
elaine: Good call — harness used a new preproc for truncation (remove html tags + whitespace collapse). I ran a quick diff: 1.2% of queries had doc trimming differences.
ben: That could shift ranks for long docs. But 3.2% ndcg drop is kinda large. Can you paste the eval command and a small failure example?
elaine: Sure: 
```bash
./eval_rerank.py 
  --model tiny-reranker-int8 
  --candidates candidates.jsonl 
  --queries queries.jsonl 
  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@1 
  --seed 42
```
One failing sample: query "how to configure sso"
candidate A (fp16): score 4.2 -> rank1
candidate B (int8): score 4.5 -> rank1 (doc shorter, stripped code block)
The gold doc was candidate A (so ndcg suffers) but model picked B consistently.
priya: Does candidate B contain repeated boilerplate? Quantization can amplify preference for shorter docs if prefix tokens get stronger weight after logit rescale.
kai: We should check tokenizer/bpe parity. Maybe the int8 model uses different tokenization shard or trimming boundary.
elaine: Tokenizer parity verified. Also ran a logits distribution check: fp16 logits mean 1.8, std 0.9; int8 mean 2.1, std 1.05. Slightly higher mean and variance.
ben: Higher variance can increase margin separations at top ranks but compress middle, affecting ndcg.
priya: Quick idea: compute stable-top1 metric (fraction of queries where top1 matches gold) and tail-ndcg (ndcg@10 excluding top1 influence). Could isolate where improvement comes from.
elaine: Ran quick numbers: stable_top1 +1.6%, tail_ndcg@10 -4.1%. So top1 gain concentrated on <5% queries but tail loss widespread.
kai: Let's run a bootstrap significance test for both metrics. If ndcg drop is significant, we block rollout.
elaine: Eval-bot queued full bootstrap run (10k boots).
eval-bot: job 90321 started — stats will be posted when done. :robot_face:
priya: Also test canonical candidate ordering: create a normalized candidate set where we sort candidates by doc_id before scoring to remove harness non-determinism.
ben: And try a simple logit rescale calibration on int8: multiply logits by alpha and add beta (tune on small-val set). Might fix tail compression.
kai: Add a secondary ablation: run quantized model but keep fp16 KV-cache for prefix embeddings (hybrid run) to see if embedding quantization drives change.
elaine: Good checklist: 1) bootstrap significance for ndcg/mrr, 2) candidate canonicalization test, 3) logit affine calibration sweep, 4) hybrid embed experiment, 5) re-run on anchor dataset (we've been using internal-sampled; need public-like anchor).
priya: For anchor, use common-gold-5k set (we have mapping). It will show if dataset selection matters.
ben: Also capture examples where top1 changed — produce a short diff: show fp16 top1 id vs int8 top1 id and tokenized length, truncation flag.
elaine: Will produce diffs and post here. If bootstrap ndcg drop is significant, we should roll back and add calibration in the quant pipeline.
kai: Agree. If it's not significant, maybe we accept slight ndcg tradeoff for top1 improvement but document impact to downstream metrics.
elaine: Posting quick sample diff (first 3):
```
query: "reset my password"
fp16_top1: doc_112 len 280 truncated=false gold=true
int8_top1: doc_47 len 34 truncated=true gold=false
----
query: "oauth callback error"
fp16_top1: doc_99 len 412 truncated=true gold=true
int8_top1: doc_99 len 412 truncated=true gold=true
----
query: "how to configure sso"
fp16_top1: doc_24 len 520 truncated=true gold=true
int8_top1: doc_8 len 76 truncated=false gold=false
```
priya: Looks like many int8 winners are short, non-gold docs. That supports the short-doc bias hypothesis.
ben: If calibration fixes it, we should add an automated lint in the quant pipeline: after quant produce a per-query logit-shift check vs baseline; if distributional drift > threshold, fail.
elaine: Ok plan set. I'll run the canonicalization and rescale experiments now, and post eval-bot results when bootstrap ends. Thanks. :thumbsup:
